speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the impact of undesirable marketing tactics for financial products, such as ambush style marketing, on less financially literate consumers; and (b) what recourse do consumers have after buying products as a result of such tactics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS has set standards of conduct for such activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS has recently issued a public consultation to strengthen these safeguards by making them mandatory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A consumer who feels he has been sold a product through inappropriate means by a representative of an FI should immediately lodge a complaint with the FI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The FI is required, by regulation, to thoroughly investigate the matter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Where the representative has been found to have mis-sold a product, the FI will offer redress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Should the consumer remain dissatisfied with the FI’s response, he can approach the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre (FIDReC) for assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: FIDReC’s mediation and adjudication services provide consumers with an accessible and affordable avenue to resolve disputes with FIs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first is that we know lots of residents who might not be familiar with English and they tend to be older residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, what are the additional safeguards put in place to help these vulnerable residents?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We do see some of these marketers doing ambush tactics in the heartlands, going after these residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, the second supplementary question is: has MAS monitored how many victims of such ambush marketing tactics have subsequently asked to withdraw their investments and, if they want to do so, are the remedial actions and recourse easily accessible to them?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to vulnerable clients, including seniors who may not be savvy with the English language, FIs must implement additional safeguards when recommending products to such clients.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS has also publicly consulted on proposals to enhance pre- and post-transaction safeguards for these vulnerable clients.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First is the strengthening of requirements to identify selected clients.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second is to require FIs to ask the selected clients to have a trusted individual to be present during the sale and advisory process.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And third, to require FIs to audio record call-backs to the selected clients and to provide the recordings to them upon request.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is reviewing the feedback from the public consultation and will produce the response when the review is completed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the Member's second supplementary question, there are many different reasons why clients may wish to withdraw their investments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: One, it may be due to the fact that they have their own preference or they may have a change of mind.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS does not have this information, but the FIs will have that information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On what recourse mechanisms customers or consumers might have, please allow me to just elaborate shortly.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Consumers who suspect any wrongdoing again should lodge a complaint with the FIs, which are required by MAS regulations to investigate and resolve these complaints promptly and also independently.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The complaint must be handled by a separate unit comprising staff who are not involved in sales.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: FIs will then review the facts and circumstances of the case in accordance with proper procedures, including interviewing the complainant and keeping the complainant apprised of the case status.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They will offer redress to consumers where their representatives are found to have committed mis-selling or other wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If the FI's response is not to the customer's satisfaction, he or she can approach FIDReC, which I mentioned.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: While MAS does not adjudicate individual cases of disagreement between consumers and FIs, MAS will review reports of breaches or misconduct and take appropriate regulatory actions against FIs or representatives found to have breached MAS regulations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With regard to the recourse on products which are not specifically fronted by FIs, for example, commodities-related products, such as gold, can I ask the Minister of State for clarification?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is the appropriate recourse via FIDReC in those types of situations?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because if I am not mistaken, when it comes to commodities-related products, it is not.
